hard_failures.name: quantifiers_formal_not_the_class_predicate
hard_failures.detail: quantifiers.formal lines 54-55 expand the class conclusion as 'not exists q in I+ with gamma subset J^-(q) intersect M' (whole-curve, single-q non-containment), and quantifiers.domains.D5 line 80 defines the bound q the same way. The class's canonical predicate is tail-based: visibility.definition lines 219-220 requires 'there exists q in I+ AND t0 in [0,T) such that the TAIL gamma([t0,T)) is contained in J^-(q) intersect M', negation_conclusion line 222 negates that tail predicate, conclusion.statement_formal line 251 uses the named predicate visible_singularity_from_I_plus, and the rev9 comment lines 17-20 states the single-q tail predicate is 'the class's only predicate'. The F0-bound authority agrees: research_map/formulation_taxonomy.yaml 276009f4 lines 63-65 ('F1 carries ONE canonical visibility predicate - the single-q tail predicate') and lines 187-193 ('Visibility uses the single-q TAIL predicate ... The set-based reading ... must never be interchanged') with D1 resolution line 69. quantifiers.formal is strictly weaker than the class conclusion: a geodesic that starts outside J^-(q) and ends inside it satisfies the artifact's own misclassification example (line 220) yet satisfies lines 54-55, so it can be a visible singularity under the class predicate while the formal clause reports none. Independently of that, the declared negation (lines 84-88) is the negation of the tail statement, not of lines 54-55: negating lines 54-55 yields 'exists q with the whole curve contained in J^-(q)', which is strictly stronger than the declared 'some geodesic is visible'. The artifact therefore contains two mutually non-equivalent formalizations of one class, and the operative one is not an expansion of the class predicate. Reproduced independently (not only by F1-review-19): probe checks C1/C2 report FAIL on the finite discriminating model (canonical_tail_visible=True vs formal_whole_curve_no_visible=True on C_disc; exact_negation_of_formal=False on C_disc) while the two predicates agree on the C_in/C_out controls and the substituted-tail negative control flips to agreement (C3 PASS).
hard_failures.fix: Rewrite quantifiers.formal and domains.D5 with the single-q tail predicate used at visibility.definition (exists q AND t0 with the tail gamma([t0,T)) contained in J^-(q)), so that negating quantifiers.formal is exactly the declared negation; or, if the whole-curve reading is intended, that is not this class (it is weaker, and not variant SET either) and must be filed as a separate statement with its own class id, which the F0 adjudication forbids pending Human PI.
hard_failures.gate_effect: G-FORM cannot accept F1 at this hash: a reviewer accept would bind a formal expansion that is not the F0-bound class predicate.

hard_failures.name: D0_binder_domain_ill_typed
hard_failures.detail: The operative quantifier binds the pair (s,delta) over D0 (lines 49, 57), but D0 line 65 is a two-member disjunction: 'Sobolev variant s > 5/2 and delta in (1/2,1), or the smooth-with-decay default'. The smooth-with-decay disjunct supplies no (s,delta) pair (data_class.regularity_class.default lines 114-115 is a C^infinity class, sobolev_variant lines 116-119 is the only branch carrying s and delta), and the genericity ambient space is declared only for the weighted Sobolev product X^{s,delta}_vac(AF) with a Frechet topology named for the smooth branch (lines 150-151, 164). An existentially quantified 'forall (s,delta) in D0' with a member that has no (s,delta) is ill-typed, and two competent readers can instantiate the class differently (all admissible regularities vs one fixed smooth regime), which is the artifact's own schema_falsifier 1 (line 282). Probe check C4: D0_is_disjunction=true, smooth_branch_supplies_s_delta_pair=false, quantifier_binds_pair_over_D0=true.
hard_failures.fix: Make the binder domain single-valued: either bind (s,delta) over the Sobolev branch only (smooth data handled by a separate, explicitly quantified branch or as a limit statement with a transfer lemma), or drop the pair binder and quantify over the regularity class as one object. The same family of statements issue is reported for F2a/F2b by other reviewers; that part is not re-litigated here.
